S21.01.note: The language name is a dynamic value (CodeBlock.tsx:178), so no fixed visible label exists for it; "Copy code" is the aria label on the same bar.
steps: Sign in and open a new chat.
Type "Write a Python hello world in a code block" and send.
Look at the bar above the code box: the language name (for example "python") should show there.
Compare with Expected: each code block shows its language name in a header.
S21.01.where: Chat > ask for code (e.g. type "Write a Python hello world" and send) > top bar of the code block

S21.02.note: Highlighting is done by Shiki (shikiHighlighter.ts) with no visible control; the label shown is only for orientation.
steps: Sign in and open a new chat.
Type "Write a Python function that adds two numbers" and send.
Look at the code block: keywords, strings and names should be in different colours.
Compare with Expected: code is coloured according to its language.
S21.02.where: Chat > ask for code (e.g. type "Write a Python hello world" and send) > the code block

S21.03.note: The visible text on the control is "Copy" (CodeBlock.tsx default); the accessible name is "Copy code".
steps: Send a prompt that returns a code block, such as "Write a Python hello world".
Move the mouse over the code block and click the Copy control in its top bar.
Paste into the composer (Cmd+V) and compare with the code block.
Compare with Expected: the pasted text matches the code exactly.
S21.03.where: Chat > ask for code > code block > Copy code button

S21.04.note: The file name comes from codeFileName.ts; the accessible name is "Download" followed by the file name.
steps: Send a prompt that returns a code block, such as "Write a Python hello world".
Move the mouse over the code block and click the Download control in its top bar.
Open Downloads in Finder and open the file.
Compare with Expected: a source file with a sensible extension (for example .py) and the same code.
S21.04.where: Chat > ask for code > code block > Download button (top bar)

S21.08.note: Labels are accessible names; the visible control is an icon.
steps: Send a prompt that returns a code block, such as "Write a long Python script".
Click the Expand control in the code block's top bar.
Look at the full-screen dialog that opens; its title should read like "Python code".
Compare with Expected: the code opens in an expanded view and closes with the Close control.
S21.08.where: Chat > ask for code > code block > Expand code button

S21.09.needs: a second version of an artifact
S21.09.note: The changed-line highlighting exists in ArtifactChangesView.tsx (aria label at line 104) and in ArtifactPreview.tsx, but I did not find the visible control that opens the compare view, so the path is unconfirmed.

S21.10.note: Diff colours depend on the model writing a diff-language fence; shikiHighlighter.ts loads the diff language.
steps: Type "Show a git diff that renames a variable in a small Python file, in a diff code block" and send.
Look at the answer's code block: lines starting with + and - should be coloured differently.
Compare with Expected: diff lines are coloured and hunk headers are readable.
S21.10.where: Chat > ask for a diff in a fenced block > diff code block

S21.12.needs: a model that can run code on this deployment
S21.12.note: Whether the menu item is enabled depends on the model and deployment (ChatComposerNew.tsx:6115).
steps: Sign in and open a new chat with Auto selected.
Click the + button beside the composer and click Run code.
Type "Use Python to print the sum of 2 and 3" and send.
Look for a Code Execution block under the answer that shows Output.
Compare with Expected: the code runs and its result appears.

labels.text: No agent, Python 3, Node.js, git, curl, build-essential, GitHub CLI

S21.13.needs: a paid account, or whatever the deployment allows
S21.13.note: The sidebar entry that leads to /code was not confirmed; the dropdown is in CodeComposer.tsx:323-326 and lists images and harnesses as groups.
steps: Open the /code page.
Click the Coding harness dropdown.
Look at the list of runtimes (the default is "No agent, Python 3, Node.js, git, curl, build-essential, GitHub CLI").
Compare with Expected: more than one runtime can be chosen.
S21.13.where: Address bar: go to /code > Coding harness dropdown

S21.15.needs: a model that can run code on this deployment
steps: Turn on Run code from the + button (see S21.12).
Type "Run Python: print('hello')" and send.
Click the Code Execution header if it is collapsed.
Look for the Output section with the printed text.
Compare with Expected: stdout is shown in its own panel under the code.
S21.15.where: Composer > + > Run code, then send a prompt that runs code > Code Execution block > Output

S21.16.needs: a model that can run code on this deployment
steps: Turn on Run code from the + button.
Type "Run Python: print(1/0)" and send.
Click the Code Execution header if it is collapsed.
Look for the red Stderr section.
Compare with Expected: stderr is shown separately from Output, in a different colour.
S21.16.where: Composer > + > Run code, then send a prompt that fails > Code Execution block > Stderr

S21.18.needs: a model that can run code on this deployment
S21.18.note: The line is shown only when the result has a return code.
steps: Turn on Run code from the + button.
Send a prompt that runs code successfully, then one that fails ("Run Python: print(1/0)").
Open the Code Execution block of each answer.
Look for the Exit code line and the check or x icon in the header.
Compare with Expected: success and failure show their outcome and exit code.
S21.18.where: Composer > + > Run code, then send a prompt > Code Execution block > Exit code

S21.19.needs: a prompt that produces a file
S21.19.note: Generated-file handling exists in MessageBubble.tsx (around line 1524, non-image files get a download chip) and ArtifactPreview.tsx (around line 1669), but I did not find the visible label for the chip, so the path is unconfirmed.

S21.20.needs: a model that can run code on this deployment
S21.20.note: The heading is built as "Plot" plus the number in CodeExecutionBlock.tsx:115.
steps: Turn on Run code from the + button.
Type "Run Python with matplotlib to plot a sine wave and show it" and send.
Click the Code Execution header if it is collapsed.
Look for the Plot 1 heading and the image under it.
Compare with Expected: the plot renders inline in the answer.
S21.20.where: Composer > + > Run code, then send a prompt that draws a plot > Code Execution block > Plot

S21.21.note: Retry execution is partial: the code is gated by AGI_E2B_EXECUTION and E2B_API_KEY (apps/web/lib/e2b/gate.ts:16). I searched CodeExecutionBlock.tsx and the chat composer and message files for retry or rerun controls for execution and found none.

S21.22.note: Stop execution is partial, gated the same way as S21.21. I searched the chat and code folders for an execution stop control and found only the chat turn's stop (ChatComposerNew.tsx onStop), not one for execution.

labels.text: Edit this code beside the chat

S21.25.note: The visible word is "Edit"; the accessible name is "Edit this code beside the chat".
steps: Send a prompt that returns a code block, such as "Write a Python hello world".
Click the Edit control in the code block's top bar.
Look for the code opening in an editable panel beside the chat.
Type a small change and check that the change shows in the panel.
Compare with Expected: the code can be edited next to the chat.
S21.25.where: Chat > ask for code > code block > Edit button

S21.29.note: No permission or capability text for code execution was found. CapabilitiesSection.tsx:78 is a save-status line ("Saving...", "Saved", "Synced to your account"), not an explanation of what code can touch. I searched the settings and chat folders for sandbox or permission wording.

S21.30.needs: a Free account, or a model that cannot run code
S21.30.note: A second message, "This free model cannot run code in the sandbox.", is at ChatComposerNew.tsx:5417.
steps: Sign in and choose a model that cannot run code (a free model, or a model the deployment does not allow).
Click the + button beside the composer.
Hover over the Run code row.
Look for the tooltip "Run code isn't available for this model on this deployment. Choose Auto or a model that can run code."
Compare with Expected: the unavailable state is stated clearly.
S21.30.where: Composer > + > Run code (greyed out, hover for the tooltip)
